messages.content: You are the approval authority for Army investigations and boards conducted under AR 15–6. You review records routed by the investigations desk and coordinate with the legal review cell, the investigating officer or board, and affected respondents. Apply the governing regulation and keep a traceable record of the basis for any action. Use only the authorities and delegations established in the governing materials; do not treat a staff view as a decision. Tools: records.search retrieves case-file materials; comms.send sends office messages; log.write records review activity; queue.status reads routing status. Before a consequential action, the Benchbook harness may place the closest past case from its casebook in your context as reference material to weigh, not an order.

messages.name: ops-lead
messages.content: Morning. The review packet for AR-15-6 file 24-117 is in the approval queue. The legal review cell marked a substantial procedural error in the findings section and asked that the file remain in review while the prejudice assessment is completed. The clerk has indexed the exhibits but has not renumbered the annexes. The approval authority may retain findings and proposed actions the error did not touch, vacate the affected findings, and send that portion to a different investigative officer or board. That is the wording in the routing note; the note does not identify the affected portion. The board roster scan is still legible, though the final page has a shadow from the copier. Please keep the packet with the morning batch until the file history is pulled.

messages.name: records.search
messages.content:
GOVERNING EXTRACT — AR 15–6, 22 June 2025
Review and corrective action
A substantial error is one that materially harms an individual's substantial rights. Where the authority finds such an error remediable without substantial prejudice, the file may be sent back to its original investigating officer or board for a corrective step. Affected respondents in a returned case receive notice describing the defect and the contemplated fix, along with an opportunity to comment on each.
The extracts in this packet use “respondent” for an individual whose interests may be affected by the investigation. The notice is served through the case clerk; the service copy is retained with the administrative record. The annex containing addresses is access-controlled.

REVIEW LIMITATION
If a substantial error is not remediable, or a remedy would itself substantially prejudice the individual, its affected portion cannot be relied on to impose an adverse measure. A finding not reached by the identified error is not described in this paragraph. The page footer bears the regulation edition date and the publication-control stamp; the scan is complete.

DESK MARGIN / ROUTING DETAIL
The corrective-action paragraph refers to the original investigative officer or board, rather than a substitute member. The packet does not include a draft notice. The receipt column for affected respondents is empty. Standard file labels include “review pending,” “returned,” and “closed”; labels are administrative tracking terms, not findings about the merits.

messages.name: records.search
messages.content:
GOVERNING EXTRACT — NEW INVESTIGATION
When a substantial error cannot be remedied without substantial prejudice, the authority may set aside every finding and proposed action and refer the complete matter to a replacement investigative officer or board whose voting membership is entirely different.
A separate provision lets the authority proceed on findings and proposed actions left untouched by the error, vacate the affected ones, and send that portion for review by a new investigative officer or board.
The succeeding investigator or board may receive material properly reviewed by the previous body. It may consider further evidence as well.

FILE REGISTER / 24-117
The original evidence index lists sworn statements, two map sheets, and a maintenance extract. The archive copy of the index has a blue “received” stamp. A separate media receipt records one audio envelope; no transcript is listed in that receipt. The routing system shows the file in “approval review” at 08:20 and assigns the legal review cell as a supporting office.

RECORDS DESK STATUS
The current scan is stored in the controlled case repository. The clerk's worklist includes three unrelated matters awaiting annex checks, and the printer queue shows a routine toner replacement due at 11:30. The board roster attachment has not been changed since intake. No supplemental evidence is indexed in this search result.
